title: Diwan al-Khansa' (collected elegies)
published_date: collected 9th c. CE; poems composed 7th c. CE

access.edition_or_version: Collected by Ibn al-Sikkit (802-858 CE); English translation by Arthur Wormhoudt, 1973
access.language_used: ar (English translation consulted via secondary scholarship)

tone_mechanisms_observed: formulaic, repeated address to the dead brother (Sakhr, Mu'awiyah)
repeated imperative to the eye to weep, descending from ritual wailing (nawh)
public and iterative mourning sustained across many poems and years
despair at irretrievable loss, with the dead kept present rather than released
short poems built on refrains of remembered detail
mechanics.emotional_progression: Summons to weep -> praise and memory of the dead -> insistence on the centrality of grief rather than resolution.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person female mourner addressing the dead and her own weeping eye.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Monorhymed Arabic verse whose repetitions function ritually; the effect is incantatory rather than progressive.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Intimate address to the dead combined with public, ritual performance for the tribe.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Arabic ritha' conventions (ritha') as studied by Stetkevych; biographical recognition via Britannica. Translation limits: formulaic repetition in Arabic reads as redundancy in English.
mechanics.copyright_note: Source text ancient and public domain; the 1973 Wormhoudt translation is copyrighted. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
